title: Kyoto show for Eisenhower, Kobe, Nagoya and a birthday in Tokyo
summary: Their unit plays a Kyoto theater for General Eisenhower, then Kobe and Nagoya, and celebrates his birthday and Jeter's son's birth at the Ernie Pyle Theater.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: So then we left Tokyo, and went to Kyoto, southern Japan, all the way down to Kyoto. We caught that fast train. The train at that time wasn't as fast as the modern trains they have now. But it was one of those kind of trains that never was off time. It always was on time. Kyoto, Japan, was a shrine city. They picked our band to appear at a theater

to do a special show for General Eisenhower. They picked our unit, -- Unit Able One was our unit. And we played this theater. And whether the General came that night, I don't know. But we played this theater in Kyoto, and we were billeted at the Kyoto Hotel and a little adjoining hotel next to it. Beautiful shrine city.
Great Caesar's, oh it's my first-- (Unintelligible.) I've got some pictures of it up there.

And after leaving there, we went to Kobe, Japan. That's the southern tip of the Honshu Island. And we played Kobe. After playing Kobe, we went down below Kobe -- not below Kobe, we went out from Kobe at another base. Then we went to one base over on the Japan Sea.
Uh-huh. When did we go to Nagoya?

Nagoya is a city where they make beautiful chinaware and cloisonne. It was on that trip, Charles, where we got it going back. But the main thing that we were doing was entertaining the troops. We had a big show in Shofan. And April 30, we were able to -- my birthday -- we played the Ernie Pyle theater, in Tokyo. And my partner Jeter got a telegram that his son was born on that same day. So we celebrated
upstairs, remember, Charles? I opened up a couple of bottles of whisky and I said, well, we can drink now. We had a few drinks.
